Copy
Copied

Elamon has two parts: this app, and elamond, a small service on the computer you want to watch. The service reads the computer\'s own counters and sends them only to phones you paired with it. If you allow it, it also lets them control the computer. It needs no root and runs as a service of your user.

2. Open the port
The openFirewall option above does it. Without the NixOS module, open the ports yourself:
firewalld is on by default here:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. If ufw is on:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. Otherwise open TCP 47823 and UDP 5353 in the one you use.

With firewalld:

TCP 47823 is the service itself. UDP 5353 is mDNS, which lets the app find the computer by itself; without it, add the computer by its address. Over a VPN such as Tailscale or WireGuard only 47823 matters, and a trusted VPN interface needs nothing.
3. Pair the phone
On the computer run:
It shows a QR code and a six-digit code, good for five minutes. Point the phone\'s camera at the QR code and open the link: that pairs in one tap.

Or in this app tap the computer under Found on this network, or Add computer and its address, and enter the code. The app first shows the computer\'s certificate digits: they must match the Certificate line on the computer.
Troubleshooting
The computer isn\'t under Found on this network

The phone and the computer have to be on the same network, with UDP 5353 open on the computer. VPNs and many guest Wi-Fi networks block this kind of discovery. Add the computer by address instead: elamond pair shows its addresses.
The app can\'t connect
Check that the service runs, and read its log:
Then check that TCP 47823 is open in the firewall and that the phone can reach the computer\'s address.
It works only while I\'m logged in
A user\'s services stop at logout unless lingering is on:
The app says the certificate changed

The service made a new certificate: its folder ~/.local/share/elamon was deleted, or the system was reinstalled. If so, forget the computer in the app and pair again. If not, something else may be answering at that address; check the network first.
No temperatures or fans
Some sensors need kernel modules. lm-sensors finds and loads them; then restart the service:
The graphics card shows no load

NVIDIA cards need NVIDIA\'s driver, whose management library the service reads. A card marked Sleeping is powered down and is left that way until a program uses it. Intel graphics don\'t report their load without extra privileges, so the app shows the clock instead.
A monitor shows no resolution
A monitor that is switched off or blanked has no mode. If no monitor shows one, the service can\'t open the graphics device: your user has to be logged in at the computer or be in the video group.
How do I unpair a phone?
In the app: the computer\'s menu, Forget computer. To also drop the phone\'s access on the computer, list the paired phones and revoke one by its ID:
4. Control panel
The Control tab starts services, plays music, switches the power profile, runs commands and powers the computer off. It\'s off until you allow it on the computer:
On NixOS, in the service\'s settings. control.users also lets power actions, the power profile and the listed system units through without a password:
Web services show up in the Control tab with their state; tap one to open it, hold it for start, stop and restart. Add them in the app, or on the computer:
Commands are defined only on the computer, so a phone can\'t run anything else. Each becomes a button in the app; its output comes back:

Elsewhere, power actions and system units need a polkit rule, because the service runs outside a login session. Without it the app marks them \"needs permission\". Save this as /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/50-elamon.rules, with your user name:
Service commands
pair a phone: shows a QR code and a code
list paired phones with their IDs
unpair one phone
unpair every phone
print one reading, to see what the service finds
the service\'s version
Service settings
Optional, in ~/.config/elamon/elamond.toml. Restart the service after a change. The defaults:
the TCP port the app connects to
the address to listen on; \"::\" covers IPv4 and IPv6
the name shown in the app; the host name when empty
announce the service on the local network, so the app finds it
milliseconds between readings
minutes of history a phone gets when it connects
The service keeps its certificate and the paired phones in ~/.local/share/elamon. Deleting that folder unpairs every phone.
Privacy

The phone talks to your computer directly, encrypted, and trusts only the certificate it saw when pairing. Nothing passes through any server, and the app has no trackers, ads or analytics. Each phone has its own key, which the computer can revoke; keys are kept out of Android backups. Unless control is turned on, the service only reads; with it on, it acts as your user, and every action is logged with the name of the phone that asked.
